title: A relatively definable function on the realisations of a simple type is a power of the successor
author: Predrag Tanovic
work: Vaught's conjecture for theories of discretely ordered structures
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that any relatively definable function f from the realisations of a simple type to itself is a power of the successor function with respect to the order that witnesses the type (statement lines 219-221). The proof first shows that f is an automorphism: surjectivity comes from saturation, injectivity from the minimum clause applied to a preimage inside a finite interval, and order preservation from a contradiction that again uses the minimum clause (proof lines 222-229). It then uses compactness to make the extension increasing, obtains an interval-isomorphism formula that holds on a cofinite tail of C and hence lies in the type, and concludes that f agrees with a fixed shift on that tail and therefore on the whole realisation set (proof lines 231-243). The step that carries the content is the last one, where the local interval behaviour is upgraded to a global description by compactness and the C-type property. H2.
